AWS 网络服务

PART II
Diving Deep into AWS Services
第二部分：深入 AWS 服务
“Big and dumb is better.” — Mark Hill

Part II of this book covers the common AWS network, storage, compute, orchestration, big data and analytics, and machine learning (ML) services. We’ll explore the inherent designs and benefits of these managed services. This part also provides guidance for how these services need to be structured in a well-architected framework to build secure, high-performing, resilient, and efficient infrastructure for a variety of applications and workloads.

本书第二部分介绍 AWS 常见的网络、存储、计算、编排、大数据与分析以及机器学习（ML）服务。我们将探讨这些托管服务内在的设计与优势。本部分还会指导你如何把这些服务按良好架构框架组织起来，为各种应用和负载构建安全、高性能、有弹性、高效的基础设施。

At the end of Part II, you will:

    了解 AWS 提供的计算服务，以及如何为不同负载识别合适规格和类型的资源，同时利用容器和其他无服务器服务把可变成本控制住
  • Use the orchestration services offered by AWS to properly decouple and scale the application on AWS, improving flexibility and performance

Chapter 9 will dive into the fully managed network services that AWS offers. You’ll discover how to use them to create a strong, resilient cloud infrastructure. We’ll begin with learning how to get started on the AWS cloud. Then, we’ll cover basic networking concepts, such as how the internet works, virtual private cloud (VPC), subnets, internet connectivity within and outside the AWS cloud, NAT gateways (a way for your cloud systems to communicate securely with the outside world), Amazon Route 53 (for managing domain names), Amazon CloudFront (to make your web services load faster), AWS Elastic Load Balancer (ELB), and Amazon API Gateway.

第 9 章将深入 AWS 提供的全托管网络服务。你将发现如何用它们构建一个强大、有弹性的云基础设施。我们先从如何上手 AWS 云开始。然后会讲基础网络概念，例如互联网如何工作、虚拟私有云（VPC）、子网、AWS 云内外的互联网连接、NAT 网关（让你的云系统与外界安全通信的一种方式）、Amazon Route 53（用于管理域名）、Amazon CloudFront（让你的 Web 服务加载更快）、AWS 弹性负载均衡器（ELB）以及 Amazon API Gateway。

Chapter 10 will explore the managed storage services provided by AWS and help you understand how to choose the right storage services for different needs. The chapter will start with Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS), Amazon Elastic File System (EFS), and Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) object store and its different classes. The chapter will then cover databases, including Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS), Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon DocumentDB, Amazon Keyspaces, Amazon Timestream, and Amazon Neptune, as well as Amazon ElastiCache, including ElastiCache for Redis and ElastiCache for Memcached.

第 10 章将探讨 AWS 提供的托管存储服务，帮助你理解如何为不同需求选择合适的存储服务。本章从 Amazon Elastic Block Store（EBS）、Amazon Elastic File System（EFS）和 Amazon Simple Storage Service（S3）对象存储及其不同存储类别讲起。随后会讲数据库，包括 Amazon Relational Database Service（RDS）、Amazon Aurora、Amazon DynamoDB、Amazon DocumentDB、Amazon Keyspaces、Amazon Timestream 和 Amazon Neptune，以及 Amazon ElastiCache（包括 ElastiCache for Redis 和 ElastiCache for Memcached）。

Chapter 11 will introduce you to the compute services that AWS offers. We’ll figure out how to choose the right kind and size of compute resources for different jobs. We’ll look at services like Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), which is like renting virtual computers in the cloud. Then we’ll talk about AWS Lambda, a special kind of on-demand computing that happens in response to events; Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR); AWS Fargate for Elastic Container Service (ECS), which manages and deploys containers; and ECS Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) cluster for running applications in containers.

第 11 章将向你介绍 AWS 提供的计算服务。我们会弄清如何为不同作业选择合适种类和规格的计算资源。我们会看 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud（EC2）这样的服务，它就像在云上租用虚拟电脑。然后谈谈 AWS Lambda——一种特殊的、按需触发、响应事件而发生的计算；Amazon Elastic Container Registry（ECR）；用于 Elastic Container Service（ECS）的 AWS Fargate（负责管理和部署容器）；以及用于在容器中运行应用的 ECS Elastic Kubernetes Service（EKS）集群。

Chapter 12 will cover the messaging, orchestration, monitoring, and access management services from AWS. These services help you manage and coordinate different tasks in your software system. We’ll talk about Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS), a way for different parts of your system to communicate indirectly; Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) for sending messages; and Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) and Amazon Kinesis, which enable different parts of your system to talk to one another. We’ll also explore AWS Step Functions to help you piece together workflows and AWS Managed Workflows to help you manage and monitor workflows. Last, we will cover Amazon CloudWatch for monitoring and debugging your cloud applications, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) for authentication and authorization over AWS resources, Amazon Cognito for managing identity pools, and AWS AppSync to orchestrate all AWS services under one GraphQL endpoint.

第 12 章将介绍 AWS 的消息、编排、监控和访问管理服务。这些服务帮你管理和协调软件系统中的不同任务。我们会谈 Amazon Simple Queue Service（SQS）——让系统不同部分间接通信的一种方式；用于发送消息的 Amazon Simple Notification Service（SNS）；以及让系统不同部分相互对话的 Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka（MSK）和 Amazon Kinesis。我们还会探讨 AWS Step Functions（帮你把工作流拼接起来）和 AWS Managed Workflows（帮你管理和监控工作流）。最后会讲 Amazon CloudWatch（监控和调试云应用）、AWS Identity and Access Management（IAM，用于对 AWS 资源做认证和授权）、Amazon Cognito（管理身份池）以及 AWS AppSync（把所有 AWS 服务编排到一个 GraphQL 端点之下）。

People interact with multiple applications (or with one another) via the internet. We first explored communication network and protocol concepts in Chapter 6; this chapter is an extension of Chapter 6 that will introduce you to the AWS networking services Amazon VPC, Amazon Route 53, AWS Elastic Load Balancer (ELB), Amazon API Gateway, and Amazon CloudFront. The goal is to help you set up your networking infrastructure on the AWS cloud as you learn about the networking concepts related to the different services and how to establish connectivity between them.

人们通过互联网与多个应用交互（或彼此交互）。我们在第 6 章首次探讨了通信网络和协议的概念；本章是第 6 章的延伸，将向你介绍 AWS 网络服务：Amazon VPC、Amazon Route 53、AWS 弹性负载均衡器（ELB）、Amazon API Gateway 和 Amazon CloudFront。目标是帮助你在 AWS 云上搭建网络基础设施，同时学习与这些服务相关的网络概念以及如何在它们之间建立连接。

Companies used to prefer setting up their own infrastructures in on-premises data centers to make their systems more reliable and safer and to ensure that they operated per business requirements, but that comes with a high cost for infrastructure management. If you are just launching your startup idea, it will likely be too costly for you to set up a personal data center. The cloud provides cost benefits (when analyzing the costs of all the resources and optimizing them to their full potential) along with a lot of flexibility. For example, it’s much harder to sell back a physical server that you bought for setting up your personal data center than it is to turn off an Amazon EC2 machine (server) in the AWS cloud.

企业过去倾向于在本地数据中心搭建自己的基础设施，以使系统更可靠、更安全，并确保按业务需求运行，但这伴随着高昂的基础设施管理成本。如果你刚要启动创业想法，自建数据中心的成本很可能太高。云不仅提供成本优势（在分析所有资源成本并把它们优化到极致时），还带来极大的灵活性。例如，把你为自建数据中心购买的物理服务器转卖出去，要比关掉 AWS 云上的一台 Amazon EC2 机器（服务器）困难得多。

AWS operates on a shared responsibility model, meaning the customer and AWS work together to make best use of services in a secure and cost-effective way, where AWS is responsible for “security of the cloud” and customers are responsible for “security in the cloud.” Before we examine AWS’s networking components, let’s dig into where these services are located and how they are segregated per customer.

AWS 采用责任共担模型，意味着客户和 AWS 协同合作，以安全、经济的方式充分利用服务：AWS 负责“云的安全”，客户负责“云中的安全”。在考察 AWS 的网络组件之前，我们先深入看看这些服务位于何处、以及如何按客户隔离。

Getting Started with AWS

To start with AWS’s cloud computing services, customers need to create an AWS account. This account is a fundamental entity in AWS that provides access to a wide range of services. It holds all the information related to the creation, management, operations, support, and billing of your AWS resources (such as compute instances, storage, networking, etc.). With an AWS account, you can provision and configure resources, monitor usage and costs, set security and access controls, and interact with various AWS services.

要使用 AWS 的云计算服务，客户需要创建一个 AWS 账户。这个账户是 AWS 中的基本实体，提供对广泛服务的访问权限。它保存与你的 AWS 资源（如计算实例、存储、网络等）的创建、管理、运维、支持和计费相关的所有信息。有了 AWS 账户，你可以开通和配置资源、监控用量和成本、设置安全和访问控制，并与各种 AWS 服务交互。

It will be very important to identify how many AWS accounts to set up. This will vary from one use case to another and will depend on the scale your organization operates on. The following are some general suggestions to consider when deciding how many AWS accounts to configure:

确定要设立多少个 AWS 账户非常重要。这会因用例而异，并取决于你组织运营的规模。在决定配置多少个 AWS 账户时，以下是一些可考虑的一般性建议：

  • Complete separation of applications. Every application is launched in a new AWS account. This option has the benefits of full separation and effective cost management of applications but presents challenges in the form of too much operational cost.
    应用完全隔离。每个应用都在一个新的 AWS 账户中启动。这种方式的好处是完全隔离、应用成本管理有效，但缺点是运维成本过高。
  • Separation of AWS accounts based on business type. For example, a cab-booking company operates in domains like cab availability, payments, and analytics. All applications related to a single business will operate in a single account, which has the advantages of correlating applications located near one another, optimizing latency, and offloading requirements of resource setup for service connection among different accounts. These applications can be segregated in Amazon VPCs or availability zones (AZs) depending on the use case.
    按业务类型划分 AWS 账户。例如，一家打车公司运营在车辆可用、支付、分析等领域。与单一业务相关的所有应用都在一个账户中运行，这样做的好处是让彼此邻近的应用互相关联、优化延迟，并免去跨账户服务连接所需的资源搭建。这些应用可以根据用例隔离到不同的 Amazon VPC 或可用区（AZ）中。
  • Separation of AWS accounts based on software domains. For example, there are separate accounts for networking, monitoring, storage, and security and auditing. This kind of setup provides for easier operations management. For example, all the networking configurations are in a single account that can be managed by the network engineering team.
    按软件域划分 AWS 账户。例如，为网络、监控、存储、安全审计分别设立账户。这种设置让运维管理更容易。例如，所有网络配置都在一个账户中，可由网络工程团队管理。

AWS recommends creating a multiaccount setup to ensure that there is clear division of responsibility while keeping future scaling of systems in mind. For example, separate networking accounts will help keep all networking configurations in a single place, with access only to the networking team. AWS offers the Landing Zone service, which provides a baseline to get started with multiaccount architecture, IAM, governance, data security, network design, and logging. AWS Landing Zone can be orchestrated by customers themselves or as a managed service. One such service, AWS Control Tower, can be used to set up initial prescriptive configurations, and further customizations can be made as organizations scale.

AWS 建议采用多账户设置，以确保职责划分清晰，同时兼顾系统未来的扩展。例如，独立的网络账户有助于把所有网络配置集中在一处，仅网络团队可访问。AWS 提供 Landing Zone 服务，为多账户架构、IAM、治理、数据安全、网络设计和日志提供起步基线。AWS Landing Zone 可以由客户自己编排，也可以作为托管服务使用。其中 AWS Control Tower 可用于设置初始的规范性配置，并可在组织扩展时做进一步定制。

AWS Regions

Once you have created an AWS account, you’re ready to launch the first server in the cloud. A very intriguing question, though, is: where is this cloud? The AWS cloud operates from a physical location, which might be near you or far from you. AWS defines the geographically distributed locations around the world where it operates data centers as AWS regions. For example, the US North Virginia region is called us-east-1. Each region is a separate and independent geographic area, isolated from other regions. You can choose the AWS region to launch resources per your business requirements, such as latency constraints or compliance regulations, or for AWS service availability in the region. For example, Netflix architecture has presence in three AWS regions, ensuring high availability even in cases of regional failure. Keeping resources at multiple locations helps build resilient systems, which we touched on in Part I. Amazon provides a complete list of regions available across the globe. There are some global services, such as AWS IAM, where region selection is not a requirement.

创建好 AWS 账户后，你就准备好在云上启动第一台服务器了。不过一个很有意思的问题是：这片云在哪里？AWS 云在一个物理位置运营，可能离你近，也可能离你远。AWS 把其在全球运营数据中心的地理位置分布定义为 AWS 区域（region）。例如，美国北弗吉尼亚区域叫 us-east-1。每个区域都是一个独立的地理区域，与其他区域隔离。你可以根据业务需求（例如延迟约束或合规法规）、或根据该区域的 AWS 服务可用性来选择启动资源的区域。例如，Netflix 架构存在于三个 AWS 区域中，即使在区域故障时也能确保高可用。把资源放在多个位置有助于构建有弹性的系统，我们在第一部分提到过这一点。Amazon 提供全球可用区域的完整列表。有些全局服务（例如 AWS IAM）不需要选择区域。

There is a possibility that not all AWS services are present in your AWS region.
有可能你的 AWS 区域中并不提供所有 AWS 服务。

AWS Availability Zones

Customers choose to deploy resources in multiple regions to improve availability, latency, and many other business use cases. A key point to note is that not everyone can afford to replicate resources in multiple AWS regions. Does that mean they must compromise application availability? Cloud providers work on a shared responsibility model, which means that to ensure a good run on the cloud, customers and cloud providers must work together. A simple example could be deploying your servers in multiple availability zones instead of just one. That way, even if one AZ goes down, there are servers operational in other AZs to serve the traffic. You can think of a single region as a cluster of data centers and each data center (or combination of data centers) as an availability zone. An AZ is physically isolated from other AZs by meaningful distance, with independent power and cooling and fast, private, fiber-optic, low-latency network connectivity. The purpose of AZs is to provide fault tolerance, resilience, and high availability by allowing you to distribute your applications and data across multiple AZs within a region. AZs are classified with suffixes to region names; for example, us-east-1a or us-east-1b are AZs within the us-east-1 region.

客户选择把资源部署到多个区域，以提升可用性、延迟以及满足许多其他业务用例。需要注意的一点是，并非人人都有能力在多个 AWS 区域复制资源。这是否意味着他们必须牺牲应用可用性？云厂商采用责任共担模型，意味着要保证在云上良好运行，客户和云厂商必须协同合作。一个简单的例子是把服务器部署到多个可用区，而不只是一个。这样，即使某个 AZ 宕机，其他 AZ 中仍有服务器在运行来服务流量。你可以把单个区域想象成一簇数据中心，而每个数据中心（或数据中心的组合）就是一个可用区。每个 AZ 与其他 AZ 之间有有意义的物理距离进行隔离，拥有独立的供电和制冷，以及快速、私密、光纤、低延迟的网络连接。AZ 的目的是让你能把应用和数据分布到一个区域内的多个 AZ 中，从而提供容错、弹性和高可用。AZ 在区域名后加后缀来命名；例如 us-east-1a 或 us-east-1b 就是 us-east-1 区域内的 AZ。

AWS Local Zones

Consider the following scenario: you are all set to launch your startup for the people of New Delhi, India. The application setup requires single-digit p99.99 latency for API operations, but the nearest AWS region is Mumbai, India. The operations are optimized well, and your use case doesn’t allow you to use precached data, such as utilizing a CDN or retrieving data from servers located at a specific AZ. How can you overcome such an issue? This can potentially be solved by placing database instances near customers, which can be achieved via AWS local zones. Local zones enable you to set up infrastructure near your customers, and the infrastructure is connected to an AWS region via a fast-paced network. We’ll also discuss potential use of AWS Local Zones in Chapter 21 while designing stock broker application.

考虑下面这个场景：你准备为印度新德里的人们推出创业产品。应用要求 API 操作的 p99.99 延迟控制在个位数毫秒，但最近的 AWS 区域是印度孟买。操作已经优化得很好，而你的用例又不允许使用预缓存数据（例如利用 CDN、或从位于特定 AZ 的服务器取数据）。你该如何解决这个问题？这有可能通过把数据库实例放在离客户近的地方来解决，而这可以通过 AWS 本地区域（Local Zone）实现。本地区域让你能在客户附近搭建基础设施，该基础设施通过高速网络连接到某个 AWS 区域。我们在第 21 章设计股票经纪应用时，也会讨论 AWS 本地区域的潜在用法。

AWS local zones are an extension of an AWS region and are designed to bring AWS services with low-latency requirements closer to specific geographic areas. Local zones are geographically separated from their parent regions and are located in metropolitan areas. They provide a subset of AWS services and are primarily intended for latency-sensitive workloads that require proximity to end users or specific on-premises resources. You can check all available locations for local zones and a list of the supported AWS services.

AWS 本地区域是 AWS 区域的延伸，旨在把有低延迟要求的 AWS 服务带到离特定地理区域更近的地方。本地区域在地理上与其父区域分离，位于大都市中。它们提供 AWS 服务的一个子集，主要面向那些需要靠近终端用户或特定本地资源的延迟敏感型负载。你可以查看本地区域的所有可用位置以及受支持的 AWS 服务清单。

AWS Edge Locations

Imagine that HBO is planning to stream a new season of Game of Thrones, and the first episode will be out on an upcoming Sunday morning at 8 A.M. Game of Thrones is popular worldwide, and the new episode is expected to be watched by many viewers in multiple countries at the same time. How can HBO ensure the best customer experience via full high-definition video quality with no video buffering? The AWS CDN service Amazon CloudFront can place the content near viewers at locations called edge locations so that customers can be served in the minimum time possible.

想象 HBO 计划流媒体播放新一季《权力的游戏》，第一集将在某个周日早上 8 点上线。《权力的游戏》在全球都很受欢迎，预计新一集在同一时刻会被多个国家的大量观众观看。HBO 如何才能通过全高清画质、无视频缓冲来确保最佳客户体验？AWS 的 CDN 服务 Amazon CloudFront 可以在被称为边缘站点（edge location）的位置把内容放到离观众近的地方，从而以最短时间服务客户。

AWS edge locations are points of presence (PoPs) distributed globally to bring AWS services closer to end users. Edge locations improve the performance of content delivery by acting as caching and content delivery endpoints for CloudFront, thus reducing latency and increasing data-transfer speeds.

AWS 边缘站点是分布在全球的接入点（PoP），用于把 AWS 服务带到离终端用户更近的地方。边缘站点通过充当 CloudFront 的缓存和内容投递端点来提升内容投递性能，从而降低延迟、提高数据传输速度。

You can think of AWS edge locations as data centers that are connected with AWS regions to support fast uploading and downloading of data. Some other services—such as Amazon Route 53, an Amazon DNS service—use the same setup for faster resolution of DNS queries. Figure 9-1 shows the connectivity of users via AWS edge locations to AWS regions.

你可以把 AWS 边缘站点想象成与 AWS 区域相连的数据中心，以支持数据的快速上传和下载。其他一些服务——例如 Amazon 的 DNS 服务 Amazon Route 53——也利用同样的设置来更快地解析 DNS 查询。图 9-1 展示了用户通过 AWS 边缘站点连接到 AWS 区域的方式。

这个高层视图介绍了 AWS 云如何搭建、以及如何让全球客户访问。下面我们直接进入如何与 AWS 云建立连接，以及云内部的各种网络组件。

Introduction to AWS Networking Services

Figure 9-1 showed how users establish connections to AWS services located within an AWS region. It’s important to understand how this accessibility is maintained and how the AWS cloud provides a similar abstraction for your private data center. This section will introduce you to offerings that AWS provides in the context of networking and connectivity.

图 9-1 展示了用户如何与位于某个 AWS 区域内的 AWS 服务建立连接。重要的是理解这种可访问性是如何维持的，以及 AWS 云如何为你的私有数据中心提供类似的抽象。本节将向你介绍 AWS 在网络和连接方面提供的产品。

Amazon VPC

Setting up your own data center could be costly in terms of both monetary costs and operations management. Amazon VPC provides a similar level of infrastructure separation to what you’d have in a personal, private data center. You can think of VPC as your personal data center located inside the AWS cloud.

自建数据中心在金钱成本和运维管理两方面都可能很昂贵。Amazon VPC 提供了与你在私有数据中心中类似级别的基础设施隔离。你可以把 VPC 想象成位于 AWS 云内部的个人数据中心。

Amazon’s VPC service allows you to create a virtual network in the cloud. It gives you control over your network environment, including selection of an IP address range, creation of subnets, configuration of route tables, and network gateways. VPC enables you to securely launch resources like Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon RDS, and AWS ELBs within a logically isolated section of the AWS cloud.

Amazon 的 VPC 服务允许你在云中创建虚拟网络。它让你掌控自己的网络环境，包括选择 IP 地址范围、创建子网、配置路由表和网络网关。VPC 让你能在 AWS 云的一个逻辑隔离区段内安全地启动 Amazon EC2 实例、Amazon RDS、AWS ELB 等资源。

This book will not outline the steps in setting up the infrastructure but will focus more on core concepts of AWS. We will provide links to AWS documentation for guidance on setup and recommend you visit the product pages for more details.
本书不会罗列搭建基础设施的具体步骤，而更聚焦 AWS 的核心概念。我们会提供 AWS 文档链接以指导搭建，并建议你访问产品页面了解更多细节。

A lot of customers use the AWS cloud. Amazon VPC plays a vital role in setting up boundaries between customer resources. AWS accounts come with one default VPC to launch resources, and more VPCs can be created per the use case requirements. There is a default limit of five VPCs per account per region, which can be increased by raising a query with AWS Support Center. We’ll dig into VPC in more detail, starting with some basic networking knowledge that will be helpful for making better decisions about how to set up your VPC.

许多客户使用 AWS 云。Amazon VPC 在客户资源之间划定边界方面起着至关重要的作用。每个 AWS 账户自带一个默认 VPC 用于启动资源，并可根据用例需求创建更多 VPC。每个账户每个区域默认限制 5 个 VPC，可以通过向 AWS 支持中心提交申请来提高。我们将更详细地深入 VPC，先从一些基础网络知识讲起，这些知识有助于你更好地决定如何搭建 VPC。

IP addresses

Let’s consider a real-world example. You’re very excited to meet a new friend in person, and both of you have agreed to meet at Cafe Delhi Heights, Third Floor, 301 and 302, Ambience Mall, Gurugram, India. However, you need a specific location—a table number in this restaurant, not just the restaurant location. This pinpointed location in the networking world is called an IP address: a unique string of characters that identifies each computer. Every device should have an IP address to connect with another device on the internet. IP addresses can be of type IPv4 or IPv6.

让我们看一个现实例子。你很兴奋要与一位新朋友见面，你们约在印度 Gurugram 的 Ambience 商场三楼 301、302 室的 Cafe Delhi Heights。然而，你需要一个具体位置——这家餐厅里的桌号，而不只是餐厅的位置。在网络世界里，这种精确定位就叫 IP 地址：一串标识每台计算机的唯一字符。每台设备都应有一个 IP 地址，才能与互联网上的另一台设备连接。IP 地址可以是 IPv4 或 IPv6 类型。

IPv4. IPv4 is a 32-bit or 4-byte address space where each byte is represented via decimal numbers (binary octet) and separated by a dot (.), such as 192.168.1.0. How can we identify which destination the traffic should be routed to? How does the postal service deliver mail to your doorstep, or how do you know to meet your new friend at table 21 at Cafe Delhi Heights? Two components are generally required for unique identification. For physical mail, these would be your zip code, postal code, or area PIN code (depending on your country) and your house number, and for meeting your new friend, they would be the restaurant location in Ambience Mall, Gurugram, and the table number inside this restaurant.

IPv4。IPv4 是一个 32 位（即 4 字节）的地址空间，每个字节用十进制数（二进制八位组）表示，并用点（.）分隔，例如 192.168.1.0。我们如何识别流量应被路由到哪个目的地？邮政服务如何把邮件送到你家门口，或者你怎么知道要在 Cafe Delhi Heights 的 21 号桌见新朋友？唯一标识通常需要两个组成部分。对实体邮件来说，这两个部分是你的邮政编码（取决于国家）和门牌号；对见新朋友来说，则是 Gurugram 的 Ambience 商场里的餐厅位置、以及餐厅内的桌号。

Similarly, two components are involved in delivering network packets to your personal computer: a network component (network ID) and a host component (host ID). For example, your office network will map to a network ID, and your personal computer will map to a host ID.

类似地，把网络数据包投递到你的个人计算机也涉及两个组成部分：网络部分（网络 ID）和主机部分（主机 ID）。例如，你的办公网络映射到一个网络 ID，你的个人计算机映射到一个主机 ID。

The division of the number of bits that should be allocated to the network ID and host ID is defined via IP classes, as shown in Figure 9-2. There are in total five IP classes from A to E, out of which Class D is reserved for multitasking and Class E is reserved for research purposes.

分配给网络 ID 和主机 ID 的位数如何划分，是通过 IP 类来定义的，如图 9-2 所示。IP 类从 A 到 E 共五类，其中 D 类保留用于多任务（组播），E 类保留用于研究。

Page 248

One difference between classes A, B, and C is the number of bits assigned to each network ID and host ID. Another is the range of IP addresses that are allowed in each class, which are listed in Table 9-1.

A、B、C 三类之间的一个区别是分配给网络 ID 和主机 ID 的位数不同。另一个区别是每类允许的 IP 地址范围不同，如表 9-1 所列。

IP address classIP range
Class A1.0.0.0−127.255.255.255
Class B128.0.0.0−191.255.255.255
Class C192.0.0.0−223.255.255.255
表 9-1。按类划分的 IPv4 地址范围。A 类：1.0.0.0–127.255.255.255；B 类：128.0.0.0–191.255.255.255；C 类：192.0.0.0–223.255.255.255。

Deciding which class suits your specific use case depends on the requirements for the number of networks and number of hosts in a network. For example, Class A provides 126 network IDs and 16,777,214 host IDs, whereas Class C provides 2,097,152 network IDs and 254 host IDs. Division of IP address or network space into network and host address is achieved via subnet masks. Class C addresses are most common for general-purpose use cases, such as home networks and small-business setups.

选择哪一类适合你的具体用例，取决于你对网络数量和每个网络中主机数量的需求。例如，A 类提供 126 个网络 ID 和 16,777,214 个主机 ID，而 C 类提供 2,097,152 个网络 ID 和 254 个主机 ID。把 IP 地址或网络空间划分为网络地址和主机地址是通过子网掩码实现的。C 类地址最常用于通用场景，例如家庭网络和小型企业组网。

As the name suggests, subnets divide the parent network into subnetworks. The subnet mask is the division of the IP address into the network and host address. It is a 32-bit number where host bits are set to 0 and network bits are set to 1. Amazon VPC logically isolates the resources at regional level, and further division into AZs can be achieved via subnets—we’ll be exploring this while creating our first VPC in follow-up sections. Figure 9-3 shows an example IPv4 address along with its subnet mask representation.

顾名思义，子网（subnet）把父网络划分为若干子网络。子网掩码就是把 IP 地址划分为网络地址和主机地址的划分方式。它是一个 32 位的数，其中主机位设为 0、网络位设为 1。Amazon VPC 在区域级别逻辑隔离资源，而进一步划分到 AZ 可以通过子网实现——我们会在后续小节创建第一个 VPC 时探索这一点。图 9-3 展示了一个 IPv4 地址及其子网掩码表示。

Page 249

A specific problem that arises with IPv4 addresses is the very limited number of addresses available in comparison to the number of devices and networks across the world. The interim solution to slow exhaustion of IPv4 addresses is via Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR).

IPv4 地址带来的一个具体问题是：与全球设备和网络的数量相比，可用地址数量非常有限。缓解 IPv4 地址耗尽的临时方案是无类别域间路由（CIDR）。

Keep in mind that the first four IP addresses and last IP address in each subnet CIDR block are reserved for special purposes and therefore can’t be assigned to hosts (or resources).
请记住，每个子网 CIDR 块中的前四个 IP 地址和最后一个 IP 地址被保留作特殊用途，因此不能分配给主机（或资源）。

CIDR is a way of representing an IP address and its subnet mask. The classless concept was introduced in 1993 to slow the exhaustion of IPv4 addresses. CIDR helps in varying subnet mask length, skipping standard division via classes. This kind of division optimizes the class space of IP addresses. You can see this represented in Figure 9-4.

CIDR 是一种表示 IP 地址及其子网掩码的方式。无类别概念于 1993 年引入，以减缓 IPv4 地址的耗尽。CIDR 允许变化子网掩码长度，跳过按类的标准划分。这种划分优化了 IP 地址的类别空间。你可以在图 9-4 中看到其表示。

However, the long-term solution is migration to IPv6 addresses.

然而，长期的解决方案是迁移到 IPv6 地址。

IPv6. IPv6 is 128 bits, which provides a much larger network space as compared to 32-bit IPv4 addresses. IPv6 is represented by eight groups of four hexadecimal digits and separated by colons, such as ab90:cd00:0000:0cef:0123:0000:211f:345d. Figure 9-5 describes a simple IPv6 notation where the site prefix represents public topology allocated by an ISP or regional internet registry; the subnet ID represents a private topology, which is internal to a specific network; and the interface ID represents a unique device identifier, which is configured via the interface’s MAC address using IEEE’s extended unique identifier (EUI-64) format.

IPv6。IPv6 为 128 位，相比 32 位的 IPv4 地址提供了大得多的网络空间。IPv6 由八组、每组四个十六进制数字表示，并用冒号分隔，例如 ab90:cd00:0000:0cef:0123:0000:211f:345d。图 9-5 描述了一种简单的 IPv6 记法：站点前缀代表由 ISP 或区域互联网注册机构分配的公共拓扑；子网 ID 代表特定网络内部的私有拓扑；接口 ID 代表唯一设备标识，它通过接口的 MAC 地址、按 IEEE 扩展唯一标识符（EUI-64）格式配置。

Page 250

Both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses can be further divided into public and private IP addresses based on their visibility. The concept of public-private is used more for IPv4 addresses, considering the limited availability of addresses. We’ll be using examples of IPv4 addresses to walk through it.

IPv4 和 IPv6 地址都可以根据可见性进一步分为公有 IP 和私有 IP。考虑到地址数量有限，公私这一概念更多用于 IPv4 地址。我们将用 IPv4 地址的例子来讲解。

Private and public IP addresses. Returning to our example, you agreed to meet your friend at a reserved table, number 21, at Cafe Delhi Heights to enjoy the restaurant’s positive vibe and food. You got curious and decided to visit the kitchen where this delicious food was prepared, but the restaurant owner denied you access, saying that only specific individuals can go to the kitchen. Here, the kitchen is private space, and the general sitting area is public space. Certainly, there are ways to get to the private space (aka the kitchen in this scenario), which we’ll explore in follow-up sections.

私有 IP 与公有 IP 地址。回到我们的例子，你和朋友约在 Cafe Delhi Heights 预订的 21 号桌，享受餐厅的氛围和美食。你好奇地想去看看制作美食的厨房，但餐厅老板拒绝你进入，说只有特定人员才能去厨房。在这里，厨房是私有空间，公共用餐区是公有空间。当然，是有办法进入私有空间（本例中即厨房）的，我们会在后续小节探讨。

Or consider your work-from-home setup: you have a router for WiFi connection, and all your devices (such as your mobile phone, office laptop, personal laptop, etc.) connect with this router to access the internet. If you run a Google search on all the devices for “What’s my IP?” you’ll get the same IP address. This IP address is called a public IP address and is assigned by the ISP. You might wonder how a single IP address can be used by multiple devices for communication; that is where NAT comes in, which we’ll discuss more in “NAT gateway.” Restarting the router might generate a different IP address, but it will still be the same across all the devices connected to the same ISP.

或者想想你的居家办公环境：你有一个无线路由器，所有设备（手机、办公笔记本、个人笔记本等）都连到这个路由器上上网。如果你在所有设备上用 Google 搜索“我的 IP 是什么”，会得到同一个 IP 地址。这个 IP 地址叫公有 IP 地址，由 ISP 分配。你可能会好奇一个 IP 地址怎么能被多台设备用来通信；这就是 NAT 的用武之地，我们会在“NAT 网关”一节详细讨论。重启路由器可能会换一个不同的 IP 地址，但在连接同一 ISP 的所有设备上它仍然是同一个。

All these devices can connect with one another without going over the internet via private IP addresses. The router assigns a private IP address to each device connected to it. Table 9-2 shows the range of addresses allowed for private IP addresses—the rest can all be used for public network space.

所有这些设备可以通过私有 IP 地址彼此通信，而无需经过互联网。路由器给连接它的每台设备分配一个私有 IP 地址。表 9-2 列出了允许用作私有 IP 地址的地址范围——其余都可用于公网空间。

IP address classIP address range
Class A10.0.0.0−10.255.255.255
Class B172.16.0.0−172.31.255.255
Class C192.168.0.0−192.168.255.255
表 9-2。按类划分的私有 IPv4 地址空间。A 类：10.0.0.0–10.255.255.255；B 类：172.16.0.0–172.31.255.255；C 类：192.168.0.0–192.168.255.255。

IP addresses are assigned dynamically from the provided IP address range upon creating an AWS resource. In case there is a requirement to associate specific IP addresses to a resource, we can use elastic IP addresses.

创建 AWS 资源时，IP 地址会从所提供的 IP 地址范围中动态分配。如果需要把特定 IP 地址绑定到某个资源，可以使用弹性 IP 地址。

Elastic IP address. An elastic IP address is a static, public IPv4 address associated with an AWS account that can be assigned to an Amazon EC2 instance or network interface. This can be used for scenarios requiring a static IP address that should not change over time. For example, an elastic IP address maintains the same IP address if an unhealthy EC2 instance is replaced by a healthy instance.

弹性 IP 地址。弹性 IP 地址是与某个 AWS 账户关联的静态公有 IPv4 地址，可以分配给 Amazon EC2 实例或网络接口。它适用于需要一个不随时间变化的静态 IP 地址的场景。例如，如果一个不健康的 EC2 实例被替换为健康实例，弹性 IP 地址保持不变。

Page 251

Note that there is an additional cost associated with elastic IP addresses. They are chargeable and are bought for a specific region; IP addresses of one region are not accessible in other regions.

请注意，弹性 IP 地址会产生额外费用。它们是收费的，并且是按特定区域购买的；一个区域的 IP 地址在其他区域不可用。

Creating an Amazon VPC

The networking ideas we discussed in the previous sections will help us set up our first VPC. The VPC wizard asks for the IPv4 CIDR block, IPv6 CIDR block, and tenancy. The IPv4 CIDR block is a required input that must be added to proceed further. The VPC can work in dual mode, operating with both IPv4 and IPv6. The allowed CIDR block for IPv4 is between /16 and /28; for IPv6, it is fixed to /64.

前面几节讨论的网络概念将帮助我们搭建第一个 VPC。VPC 向导要求输入 IPv4 CIDR 块、IPv6 CIDR 块和租户隔离。IPv4 CIDR 块是必填项，必须填写才能继续。VPC 可以双栈模式工作，同时使用 IPv4 和 IPv6。IPv4 允许的 CIDR 块范围是 /16 到 /28；IPv6 则固定为 /64。

You’ll need to consider the following points for the CIDR block:

关于 CIDR 块，你需要考虑以下几点：

  • Creating a VPC requires an initial IPv4 CIDR block, although you might have a use case to just use an IPv6 address space. VPC supports both IPv4 and IPv6 address spaces in a single VPC, which can be specified during creation.
    创建 VPC 需要一个初始 IPv4 CIDR 块，尽管你的用例可能只想用 IPv6 地址空间。VPC 在单个 VPC 中同时支持 IPv4 和 IPv6 地址空间，可在创建时指定。
  • The CIDR block should be specified from the RFC 1918 range, and it is recommended to use a private IP address range, although public can also be chosen.
    CIDR 块应从 RFC 1918 范围中指定，建议使用私有 IP 地址范围，不过也可以选择公有范围。
  • The size of the CIDR block can’t be changed once created. Customers should carefully plan the size of CIDR considering future needs to avoid hurdles or rework in the future. In short, bigger CIDR blocks can be chosen to have more flexibility in the future if you’re not able to gather concrete details now.
    CIDR 块的大小一旦创建就不能更改。客户应考虑未来需求，仔细规划 CIDR 大小，以避免日后遇到障碍或返工。简而言之，如果你现在无法收集到具体细节，可以选更大的 CIDR 块，以便未来有更大灵活性。
  • The CIDR block should not overlap with existing CIDR blocks associated with VPCs. This is also essential for using services like VPC peering and AWS Direct Connect; the CIDR blocks should not overlap across the VPCs.
    CIDR 块不应与已有关联到 VPC 的 CIDR 块重叠。这对于使用 VPC 对等连接、AWS Direct Connect 等服务也很重要；各 VPC 之间的 CIDR 块不应重叠。
  • You can associate up to five additional CIDR blocks to a VPC (this is a soft limit and can be adjusted up to 50); the additional CIDR blocks’ ranges should be strictly smaller than the primary CIDR block.
    你可以为一个 VPC 关联最多 5 个额外 CIDR 块（这是一个软限制，可调高到 50）；这些额外 CIDR 块的范围应严格小于主 CIDR 块。
Soft limit means the limit is adjustable and can be increased by following AWS Service Quotas or with help of the AWS support team.
软限制意味着该限制是可调整的，可以通过 AWS Service Quotas 或在 AWS 支持团队帮助下提高。

Next, we need to consider tenancy. Let’s go back to our real-world example. There are two ways to book Cafe Delhi Heights for meeting your new friend. The first option is to book the entire restaurant if this is a top-secret meeting and you don’t want any other people there during your booked time. This is called dedicated tenancy. The second option is to reserve a table for two—other available tables can be booked by other people. This is called shared tenancy. Because of the cost, it’s logical to go with the second option unless there is a specific reason not to, such as a secret meeting. The same concept applies when we request servers from AWS. The instances can run either on shared hardware (other people’s instances can run on the same hardware via virtualization) or on dedicated hardware where your instances are separated from other customer’s resources, depending on your business needs. This option can be selected at the time of creating the VPC, and all the instances launched in the VPC are created with the same option by default, unless overridden.

接下来需要考虑租户隔离（tenancy）。回到现实例子。预订 Cafe Delhi Heights 见新朋友有两种方式。第一种是包下整个餐厅——如果这是一次绝密会面，你不希望在预订时段有其他人在场。这叫专用租户（dedicated tenancy）。第二种是预订一张两人桌——其他空桌可以被别人预订。这叫共享租户（shared tenancy）。出于成本考虑，选第二种是合乎逻辑的，除非有特殊原因不这么做（例如秘密会面）。当我们向 AWS 请求服务器时，同样的概念也适用。实例可以运行在共享硬件上（通过虚拟化，别人的实例可以跑在同一硬件上），也可以运行在专用硬件上（你的实例与其他客户资源隔离），取决于业务需求。这个选项可以在创建 VPC 时选择，VPC 中启动的所有实例默认都使用同一选项，除非另行覆盖。

Page 252
AWS provides multiple tools for creating resources, such as the AWS CLI, and the AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK), or via the AWS Console. As a beginner, you can start by experimenting with the AWS Console, but as systems scale, we recommend maintaining a code repository to provision any AWS resources, which is popularly known as infrastructure-as-code (IaC). This could help on multiple fronts, such as replicating the same resources in another region or maintaining an infrastructure audit.
AWS 提供多种创建资源的工具，例如 AWS CLI、AWS Cloud Development Kit（CDK），或通过 AWS 控制台。作为初学者，你可以先从 AWS 控制台上手，但随着系统扩展，我们建议维护一个代码仓库来开通任何 AWS 资源，这就是俗称的基础设施即代码（IaC）。这能在多方面带来帮助，例如在另一个区域复制相同资源、或维护基础设施审计。

The next step in VPC configuration is setting up subnets. Subnets separate resources across multiple AZs.

VPC 配置的下一步是设置子网。子网把资源分隔到多个 AZ 中。

Subnets

As we’ve mentioned, subnet means a subnetwork: a logical subdivision of the IP address range inside the VPC CIDR block. Why should you divide network space into multiple subnetworks? The general idea of separation of resources per AZ is to ensure high application availability. Each subnet is associated with an AZ within an AWS region. By associating resources to specific subnets, we ensure that resources are launched into that AZ. One interesting fact about mapping subnets to AZs is it can vary from customer to customer: the us-east-1a AZ for you can be us-east-1b for your friend. AWS abstracts out these details from customers to ensure uniform allocation (per availability) of resources.

如前所述，子网就是子网络：VPC CIDR 块内 IP 地址范围的逻辑细分。为什么要把网络空间划分为多个子网络？按 AZ 隔离资源的总体思路是为了确保应用高可用。每个子网都与 AWS 区域内的某个 AZ 关联。通过把资源关联到特定子网，我们确保资源被启动到那个 AZ。关于子网到 AZ 的映射，一个有趣的事实是它因客户而异：你的 us-east-1a 对朋友可能是 us-east-1b。AWS 对客户屏蔽了这些细节，以确保资源（按可用性）均匀分配。

Each subnet should be assigned a CIDR block similar to the VPC; the CIDR block to be assigned can be the same as the VPC CIDR block or a subset of it. The key point is that the CIDR block across the subnets inside your VPC should not overlap. The first four and the last IP address in each subnet CIDR block are reserved and can’t be assigned to resources.

每个子网都应像 VPC 一样分配一个 CIDR 块；要分配的 CIDR 块可以与 VPC CIDR 块相同，也可以是其子集。关键在于 VPC 内各子网之间的 CIDR 块不应重叠。每个子网 CIDR 块中的前四个和最后一个 IP 地址被保留，不能分配给资源。

The subnet can be a public subnet or a private subnet, depending on its connectivity to the internet. Public and private subnets look similar; the difference lies in their accessibility to the internet. For example, a web application’s servers can be placed in a public subnet so that the application is accessible to the general public via the internet, and the database servers can be placed in a private subnet to limit accessibility from the general public; see Figure 9-6 for reference. You were denied access to the kitchen at Cafe Delhi Heights because it’s located in a private space (or private subnet), although you can freely roam in the general sitting area as this is public space or public subnet.

子网可以是公有子网或私有子网，取决于它与互联网的连接情况。公有子网和私有子网看起来相似；区别在于它们对互联网的可访问性。例如，Web 应用的服务器可以放在公有子网中，以便公众能通过互联网访问应用；数据库服务器可以放在私有子网中，以限制公众访问；参见图 9-6。你被拒绝进入 Cafe Delhi Heights 的厨房，是因为它位于私有空间（即私有子网），而你可以在公共用餐区自由走动，因为那是公有空间（即公有子网）。

Page 253

The resources in the public subnet can access the internet because of the presence of a direct route to an internet gateway (shown as igw-id in the custom route table in Figure 9-6), whereas resources in the private subnet require a NAT service or a NAT instance to access the internet (nat-gateway-id entry in the route table). Later sections in this chapter will provide more details on network access control lists (NACLs), route tables, the NAT gateway, and the internet gateway. The key point is that the direct route to the internet gateway is the only differentiating factor between public and private subnets. A subnet with resources having a public IPv4 address but no direct route to the internet gateway is called a private subnet.

公有子网中的资源之所以能访问互联网，是因为存在一条到互联网网关的直达路由（在图 9-6 的自定义路由表中显示为 igw-id），而私有子网中的资源需要 NAT 服务或 NAT 实例才能访问互联网（路由表中的 nat-gateway-id 条目）。本章后续小节会详细介绍网络访问控制列表（NACL）、路由表、NAT 网关和互联网网关。关键在于：到互联网网关的直达路由是公有子网与私有子网之间唯一的区别因素。一个子网中的资源即使有公有 IPv4 地址、但没有到互联网网关的直达路由，也称为私有子网。

When setting up your VPCs and subnets inside your AWS account, consider these following best practices:

在 AWS 账户内搭建 VPC 和子网时，请考虑以下最佳实践：

  • Use multiple subnets. Create multiple subnets within different AZs to achieve fault tolerance and high availability.
    使用多个子网。在不同 AZ 中创建多个子网，以实现容错和高可用。
Page 254
  • Isolate resources. Use separate subnets for different types of resources to improve security and network segmentation.
    隔离资源。为不同类型的资源使用独立子网，以提升安全性和网络分段。
  • Separate public and private subnets. Place resources with public access in public subnets and sensitive resources in private subnets.
    分离公有子网和私有子网。把有公有访问需求的资源放在公有子网，把敏感资源放在私有子网。

VPC provides a logically isolated network in the AWS cloud, but how does this network connect with the internet? Or how can internet traffic access the resources located in the subnets? Let’s discuss that next.

VPC 在 AWS 云中提供了一个逻辑隔离的网络，但这个网络如何与互联网连接？或者互联网流量如何访问位于子网中的资源？下面我们讨论这个问题。

Internet Connectivity

Routing traffic and securing resources are achieved via components like route tables, internet gateways, and security groups, which we’ll focus on in this section.

路由流量和保护资源是通过路由表、互联网网关和安全组等组件实现的，本节将重点介绍它们。

Route Tables

In the AWS cloud, you just need to configure required routes in the route table; you don’t have to worry about setting up a router. A route table is a collection of rules, called routes, that determine where network traffic from your subnet or gateway is directed. We can assume that AWS internally maintains a router to facilitate this routing.

在 AWS 云中，你只需在路由表中配置所需路由；不必操心搭建路由器。路由表是一组规则（称为路由）的集合，决定来自子网或网关的网络流量被导向何处。我们可以认为 AWS 在内部维护了一台路由器来完成这种路由。

Every subnet should be associated with a route table, and the main route table is created implicitly to provide private access among the subnets. You should create more custom route tables as required and assign them to subnets—note that the same route table can be associated with multiple subnets. The key consideration here should be to create a route table for clear division of routing responsibility; this helps provide better maintainability and readability of routes by not overcrowding a single route table.

每个子网都应关联一个路由表，主路由表是隐式创建的，用于在各子网之间提供私有访问。你应根据需要创建更多自定义路由表并分配给子网——注意同一个路由表可以关联多个子网。这里的关键考虑是：为清晰划分路由职责而创建路由表；这有助于避免单个路由表过于臃肿，从而提升路由的可维护性和可读性。

There are two kinds of route tables: main route tables and custom route tables. The main route table automatically comes with a VPC and by default contains the first entry for local routing in the VPC, which helps resources in different subnets establish connectivity with one another. Every creation of a subnet leads to implicit association to the main route table. If required, customers can create a custom route table and explicitly associate it to a subnet.

路由表有两种：主路由表和自定义路由表。主路由表随 VPC 自动生成，默认包含 VPC 内本地路由的第一条条目，帮助不同子网中的资源相互建立连接。每次创建子网都会隐式关联到主路由表。如有需要，客户可以创建自定义路由表并显式关联到子网。

You need to consider the following about the main route table:

关于主路由表，你需要考虑以下几点：

  • It can’t be deleted, and a custom route table can’t be set as the main route table, though the main route table can be replaced with a custom route table for subnet association.
    它不能被删除，自定义路由表也不能被设为主路由表，不过可以把主路由表替换为自定义路由表来做子网关联。
Page 255
  • You can add additional routes to the main table—our recommendation would be to avoid this and create custom route tables for adding custom routes.
    你可以向主表添加额外路由——但我们建议不要这样做，而是创建自定义路由表来添加自定义路由。
  • The configured routes are general-purpose routes and might not be the optimal security configuration for all use cases. Audit the routes before using them in production environments.
    所配置的路由是通用路由，未必是所有用例的最佳安全配置。在生产环境使用之前，请审计这些路由。

Custom route tables don’t contain any routes by default and should be updated per the requirements for network traffic routing. Custom route tables can be deleted, unlike the main route table, though there should be no subnet associations for this operation to be successful.

自定义路由表默认不包含任何路由，应根据网络流量路由的需求来更新。与主路由表不同，自定义路由表可以被删除，不过要成功删除，前提是它没有关联任何子网。

Now that you know the two types of route tables and their purposes, let’s see how routes are added and what they look like. There are two important inputs in the route table (see Table 9-3 for an example):

现在你了解了两种路由表及其用途，下面看看路由如何添加、长什么样。路由表中有两个重要输入（示例见表 9-3）：

  • Destination. Added as CIDR; basically, a range of IP addresses that specifies where the network packets should go, such as 10.0.0.0/16.
    目的地（Destination）。以 CIDR 形式添加；基本上就是一段 IP 地址范围，指定网络数据包应去往何处，例如 10.0.0.0/16。
  • Target. Specifies how the network packets will reach the destination, such as gateway, network interface, or a connection—for example, internet gateway (IGW) for routing traffic to the internet or VPC peering connection.
    目标（Target）。指定网络数据包如何到达目的地，例如网关、网络接口或一条连接——例如把流量路由到互联网的互联网网关（IGW），或 VPC 对等连接。
DestinationTarget
VPC CIDRLocal
0.0.0.0/0igw-id
表 9-3。通过 IGW 连接互联网的路由表。目的地为 VPC CIDR 时，目标为 Local（本地）；目的地为 0.0.0.0/0 时，目标为 igw-id（互联网网关）。

Route tables direct network traffic in and out of a subnet, but they don’t apply any security filters on this traffic. AWS provides software firewalls, security groups (SGs), and NACLs to implement traffic filters, which are useful for controlling the network traffic permissions. These components help control the traffic that can flow in and out of the VPC.

路由表引导网络流量进出子网，但不对这些流量施加任何安全过滤。AWS 提供软件防火墙、安全组（SG）和 NACL 来实现流量过滤，它们用于控制网络流量权限。这些组件帮助控制可以进出 VPC 的流量。

Security Groups

SGs define the rules for the traffic allowed to (and from) the resources. SGs are created at the VPC level and assigned at an instance level, controlling inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level based on protocols, ports, and IP addresses. Your EC2 instance can have one or more SGs. There will always be one SG associated to an instance, and, if not created, a default SG will be associated, which is created at the time of VPC creation.

安全组定义允许进出资源的流量规则。SG 在 VPC 级别创建，在实例级别分配，基于协议、端口和 IP 地址在实例级别控制入站和出站流量。你的 EC2 实例可以有一个或多个 SG。一个实例总会关联一个 SG；如果没有创建，则会关联一个默认 SG，该默认 SG 在 VPC 创建时生成。

Page 256

To secure and limit access for incoming and outgoing traffic to instances, you need to add inbound and outbound rules to your SG. Inbound rules define traffic that is allowed to the instance, and outbound rules define traffic that is allowed from the instance.

为了保护并限制进出实例的流量，你需要向 SG 添加入站和出站规则。入站规则定义允许进入实例的流量，出站规则定义允许从实例发出的流量。

Keep in mind the following facts about SGs:

请记住关于 SG 的以下事实：

  • SGs are stateful. For example, you fire one request from your personal laptop to an EC2 instance to get some data, and your IP address is added as part of the inbound rules. You’ll get a response back even if there are no outbound rules included for your personal laptop. In short, rules allowed in one direction will automatically be allowed in the opposite direction; there is no requirement to explicitly add them.
    SG 是有状态的。例如，你从个人笔记本向某 EC2 实例发一个请求取数据，你的 IP 被加入入站规则。即使没有为你的笔记本配置出站规则，你也会收到响应。简言之，一个方向允许的规则会自动在反方向允许；无需显式添加。
  • You can’t delete the default SG. Our recommendation is to create a custom SG as needed. Multiple SGs can be associated to an instance, but you should create SGs keeping future scale in mind. For example, you should avoid duplicate-rules SGs and reuse wherever possible.
    你不能删除默认 SG。我们建议按需创建自定义 SG。一个实例可以关联多个 SG，但创建 SG 时应考虑未来扩展。例如，应避免规则重复的 SG，并尽可能复用。
  • You should only add required access and not overexpose the resources. For example, for SSH connections, only allow Port 22 for a set of IP addresses and not the entire internet.
    你应只添加所需的访问权限，不要过度暴露资源。例如，对 SSH 连接，只允许一组 IP 地址访问 22 端口，而不是整个互联网。
  • SGs don’t provide an option to define explicit deny rules. All the rules that don’t match the allowed-rules condition are implicitly denied access to resources.
    SG 不提供定义显式拒绝规则的选项。所有不匹配允许规则条件的流量，都被隐式拒绝访问资源。

For each rule added as part of the inbound or outbound rules, you’ll need to specify the following parameters, as shown in Table 9-4:

对于作为入站或出站规则添加的每条规则，你需要指定以下参数，如表 9-4 所示：

  • Type. This represents the type of traffic. AWS determines the protocol and port range automatically on the basis of the chosen type value. There is also a custom type to add custom values, such as for port range.
    类型（Type）。代表流量类型。AWS 根据所选类型自动确定协议和端口范围。还有一个自定义类型，可添加自定义值，例如端口范围。
  • Source or destination. The source attribute is added for inbound rules, and the destination attribute is added for outbound rules. Here, you can add specific IP addresses, complete CIDR blocks, or other security groups.
    源或目的地。入站规则添加 source 属性，出站规则添加 destination 属性。这里可以添加特定 IP 地址、完整 CIDR 块或其他安全组。
  • Description. It is helpful to identify why a certain rule is added or what purpose it solves. This is an optional field, but we recommend using it for easy future reference.
    描述（Description）。有助于识别为何添加某条规则、或它解决什么目的。这是可选字段，但我们建议填写，便于日后查阅。
TypeProtocolPort rangeDestinationDescription
SSHTCP22117.212.92.68Test SSH rule
表 9-4。SG 出站规则示例。类型 SSH、协议 TCP、端口范围 22、目的地 117.212.92.68、描述 Test SSH rule（测试 SSH 规则）。
Page 257

Network Access Control Lists

NACLs are stateless packet filters that are attached at the subnet level. Unlike SGs, NACLs provide the ability to add, allow, or deny rules for outbound or inbound traffic at the subnet level. You can think of them as an additional layer of security on top of SGs, which block the traffic if SGs are too flexible.

NACL 是无状态的数据包过滤器，挂载在子网级别。与 SG 不同，NACL 提供在子网级别添加入站或出站流量的允许/拒绝规则的能力。你可以把它们看作 SG 之上的一层额外安全防线，当 SG 过于宽松时由它来阻断流量。

Thinking back to our example of the Cafe Delhi Heights kitchen, imagine there are individual chefs in the kitchen—you may be allowed to enter the kitchen, but a chef may still refuse to talk to you.

回想 Cafe Delhi Heights 厨房的例子，想象厨房里有各位厨师——你可能被允许进入厨房，但某位厨师仍可能拒绝和你说话。

There are a few key things you need to remember about NACLs:

关于 NACL，有几点需要记住：

  • NACLs are stateless. Customers need to add explicit rules for both inbound and outbound traffic to allow or deny actions.
    NACL 是无状态的。客户需要为入站和出站流量都添加显式规则来允许或拒绝动作。
  • Amazon VPC comes with a default NACL. The default will be attached to all the subnets inside the VPC, and it allows all inbound/outbound traffic. For fine-grained traffic control, you can create a custom NACL or modify rules in an existing one—our recommendation is to create custom NACLs as needed.
    Amazon VPC 自带一个默认 NACL。该默认 NACL 会挂载到 VPC 内所有子网，并允许所有入站/出站流量。要做细粒度流量控制，你可以创建自定义 NACL 或修改现有 NACL 的规则——我们建议按需创建自定义 NACL。
  • NACLs define inbound or outbound rules to allow or deny actions. The rules will be evaluated in sequence, and once a particular rule succeeds, all the rules in sequence following it will be skipped. If none of the rules succeed, then a final rule marked as * will evaluate it as a deny action.
    NACL 定义入站或出站规则来允许或拒绝动作。规则按顺序求值，一旦某条规则命中，其后按顺序的所有规则都会被跳过。如果没有任何规则命中，则最后一条标记为 * 的规则会把它判定为拒绝动作。

For each inbound or outbound rule, you’ll need to specify the following parameters, as shown in Table 9-5:

对于每条入站或出站规则，你需要指定以下参数，如表 9-5 所示：

  • Rule number. The rule number is the sequence of numbers in which rules are evaluated. It can be numbered from 1 to 32766.
    规则编号。规则编号是规则被求值的顺序号。编号范围可从 1 到 32766。
  • Type. Type represents the type of traffic. Based on the chosen type, AWS prepopulates the protocol and port range. A custom protocol and port range can also be added per the selected type.
    类型。代表流量类型。根据所选类型，AWS 预填协议和端口范围。也可以根据所选类型添加自定义协议和端口范围。
  • Source. Source represents inbound rules added as a CIDR block.
    源（Source）。代表以 CIDR 块形式添加的入站规则。
  • Destination. Destination represents outbound rules added as a CIDR block.
    目的地（Destination）。代表以 CIDR 块形式添加的出站规则。
  • Allow or deny. For every rule, an explicit action should be added to “allow” or “deny.” This action determines if traffic is allowed or denied.
    允许或拒绝。每条规则都应显式添加“允许”或“拒绝”动作。该动作决定流量是被允许还是拒绝。
